children.heading: In general
children.text: Any adversely affected worker covered by a certification issued under subpart A of this part may file an application for a relocation allowance with the Secretary, and the Secretary may grant the relocation allowance, subject to the terms and conditions of this section.

children.heading: Conditions for granting allowance
children.text: A relocation allowance may be granted if all of the following terms and conditions are met:

children.heading: Assist an adversely affected worker
children.text: The relocation allowance will assist an adversely affected worker in relocating within the United States.

children.heading: Local employment not available
children.text: The Secretary determines that the worker cannot reasonably be expected to secure suitable employment in the commuting area in which the worker resides.

children.heading: Total separation
children.text: The worker is totally separated from employment at the time relocation commences.
has obtained suitable employment affording a reasonable expectation of long-term duration in the area in which the worker wishes to relocate; or
has obtained a bona fide offer of such employment.

children.heading: Application
children.text: The worker filed an application with the Secretary before—
the 425th day after the date of the certification under subpart A of this part; or
the 425th day after the date of the worker’s last total separation; or
the date that is the 182d day after the date on which the worker concluded training, unless the worker received a waiver under section 2291(c) of this title.

tree.heading: Amount of allowance
tree.text: The relocation allowance granted to a worker under subsection (a) includes—

children.text: 90 percent of the reasonable and necessary expenses (including, but not limited to, subsistence and transportation expenses at levels not exceeding those allowable under section 2296(b)(1) and (2) of this title specified in regulations prescribed by the Secretary) incurred in transporting the worker, the worker’s family, and household effects; and
a lump sum equivalent to 3 times the worker’s average weekly wage, up to a maximum payment of $1,250.

tree.heading: Limitations
tree.text: A relocation allowance may not be granted to a worker unless—

children.text: the relocation occurs within 182 days after the filing of the application for relocation assistance; or
the relocation occurs within 182 days after the conclusion of training, if the worker entered a training program approved by the Secretary under section 2296(b)(1) and (2) of this title.

notes.heading: Termination of Assistance
notes.text: For termination of assistance under this part after June 30, 2022, see Termination Date note below.
